Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/upper-incomplete-gamma](#QM-3-upper-incomplete-gamma), [QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying), `tauceti:TauCeti.regularizedGamma`, `tauceti:TauCeti.lowerIncompleteGamma_eq_integral`, `mathlib:CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0`, `mathlib:EisensteinSeries.summable_norm_eisSummand`.

Named declarations and API:

- `maassPoincareSeries` (data): Q(−m, k, N; τ) = Σ_{A ∈ Γ∞\Γ₀(N)} (ψ_m|_{2−k}A)(τ).
- `maassPoincareSeed` (data): ψ_m(τ) = P(k−1, 4πm Im τ)·e(−mτ).
- `maassPoincareSeed_eq` (characterisation): ψ_m = e(−mτ) − Γ(k−1, 4πmv)e(−mτ)/(k−2)!.
- `maassPoincareSeries_summable` (other): Absolute, locally uniform convergence with all derivatives.
- `maassPoincareSeries_toHarmonic` (constructor): Q(−m, k, N) as an element of H_{2−k}^+(Γ₀(N)) (QM.3/maass-poincare-series-harmonic).

Unit tests:

- `maassPoincare_seed_test` (computation): ψ_m(τ) = e(−mτ) − Γ(k−1, 4πmv)e(−mτ)/(k−2)! for every τ.
- `maassPoincare_mem_plusSpace_test` (characterisation): Q(−m, k, N) underlies an element of H_{2−k}^+(Γ₀(N)).
- `maassPoincare_constant_term_test` (computation): For N = 1, m = 1, k = 12 the holomorphic part has constant term −65520/691.
- `maassPoincare_not_weaklyHolomorphic_test` (non-example): Q(−m, k, N) is not holomorphic: ξ_{2−k}Q(−m, k, N) = (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!·P(m, k, N) ≠ 0 whenever S_k(Γ₀(N)) ≠ 0 and P(m, k, N) ≠ 0 (e.g. N = 1, k = 12, m = 1).

Acceptance checks:

- The identity term of Q(−m, k, N) is q^{−m} − Γ(k−1, 4πmv)q^{−m}/(k−2)!, matching the leading terms q^{−m} of Q⁺ and −Γ(k−1, 4πmy)q^{−m}/(k−2)! of Q⁻ in BOR Prop. 6.2.
- For N = 1, m = 1, k = 12: the constant term of the holomorphic part is −65520/691 ≈ −94.8191 (BOR Prop. 6.2; numerically confirmed), and a⁺(1) ≈ −1842.89472.

Atlas planet: **Maass–Poincaré series**.

<a id="QM-3-maass-poincare-series-harmonic"></a>

### Q(−m, k, N) is a harmonic Maass form in H_{2−k}^+

**Theorem** (`QM.3/maass-poincare-series-harmonic`). For N ≥ 1, even k ≥ 4, m ≥ 1: Q(−m, k, N) ∈ H_{2−k}^+(Γ₀(N)); its principal part at ∞ is q^{−m} + a constant, and at every cusp of Γ₀(N) inequivalent to ∞ its principal part is constant (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Prop. 6.2, first assertion).

Ambient hypotheses: As in QM.3/maass-poincare-series..

Sources: [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), Prop. 6.2, p. 15; [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Remark 3.10, p. 15.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/maass-poincare-series](#QM-3-maass-poincare-series), [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form), [QM.3/laplacian-slash-equivariance](#QM-3-laplacian-slash-equivariance), [QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying), [QM.3/plus-space-principal-part-characterisation](#QM-3-plus-space-principal-part-characterisation).

Acceptance checks:

- For N = 1 the principal part is q^{−m} + a⁺(0).

<a id="QM-3-xi-maass-poincare-series"></a>

### ξ_{2−k}Q(−m, k, N) = (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!·P(m, k, N)

**Theorem** (`QM.3/xi-maass-poincare-series`). For N ≥ 1, even k ≥ 4, m ≥ 1: ξ_{2−k}(Q(−m, k, N)) = ((4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!)·P(m, k, N) (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades §6.2).

Ambient hypotheses: As in QM.3/maass-poincare-series..

Sources: [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), §6.2, p. 16.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/maass-poincare-series](#QM-3-maass-poincare-series), [QM.3/holomorphic-poincare-series](#QM-3-holomorphic-poincare-series), [QM.3/xi-slash-equivariance](#QM-3-xi-slash-equivariance), [QM.3/nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying](#QM-3-nonholomorphic-fourier-basis-decaying), [QM.3/xi-map](#QM-3-xi-map).

Acceptance checks:

- Consistent with QM.3/xi-fourier-expansion: a⁻(−m) = −1/(k−2)! gives leading coefficient (4πm)^{k−1}/(k−2)!.
- BOR's display: ξ_{2−k}(Q(−m, k, N; z)) = (4π)^{k−1}m^{k−1}/(k−2)!·P(m, k, N; z).

<a id="QM-3-bessel-j-bromwich-integral"></a>

### The vertical-line integral for J_ν

**Lemma** (`QM.3/bessel-j-bromwich-integral`). For real x > 0, real c > 0 and ν ∈ ℂ with Re ν > 0: J_ν(x) = (x/2)^ν·(1/(2π))∫_{−∞}^{∞}(c + iy)^{−ν−1}exp(c + iy − x²/(4(c + iy)))dy, i.e. J_ν(x) = (x/2)^ν(1/(2πi))∫_{c−i∞}^{c+i∞}t^{−ν−1}exp(t − x²/(4t))dt, the integral converging absolutely (t^{−ν−1} the principal power). This is the vertical-line form of Schläfli's loop integral (DLMF 10.9.19) and the J-analogue of QM.2/modified-bessel-i-bromwich-integral.

Ambient hypotheses: x > 0, c > 0, Re ν > 0..

Sources: [dlmf-chapter-10](#reference-dlmf-chapter-10), §10.9(ii), equation 10.9.19.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.2/bromwich-integral-reciprocal-gamma](#QM-2-bromwich-integral-reciprocal-gamma), [QM.2/bessel-function-j](#QM-2-bessel-function-j).

Acceptance checks:

- Replacing x by ix formally turns it into QM.2/modified-bessel-i-bromwich-integral.
- ν = 1/2: both sides equal √(2/(πx))·sin x.

<a id="QM-3-holomorphic-poincare-series-fourier-expansion"></a>

### Fourier coefficients of holomorphic Poincaré series

**Theorem** (`QM.3/holomorphic-poincare-series-fourier-expansion`). For even k ≥ 4 and m, N ≥ 1: P(m, k, N) = q^m + Σ_{n≥1} a(m, k, N; n)q^n with a(m, k, N; n) = 2π(−1)^{k/2}(n/m)^{(k−1)/2} Σ_{c>0, N|c} K(m, n, c)/c · J_{k−1}(4π√(mn)/c) for n ≥ 1 (the q^m term included in the n = m term by the Kronecker delta convention of BOR (6.5)); and P(−m, k, N) = q^{−m} + Σ_{n≥1} a(−m, k, N; n)q^n with a(−m, k, N; n) = 2π(−1)^{k/2}(n/m)^{(k−1)/2}Σ_{c>0, N|c} K(−m, n, c)/c · I_{k−1}(4π√(mn)/c) (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Prop. 6.1).

Ambient hypotheses: k even ≥ 4, m ≥ 1, N ≥ 1; J_ν = QM.2/bessel-function-j, I_ν = QM.2/modified-bessel-function-i; a(±m, k, N; n) real..

Sources: [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), Prop. 6.1, p. 15.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/holomorphic-poincare-series](#QM-3-holomorphic-poincare-series), [QM.3/classical-kloosterman-sum](#QM-3-classical-kloosterman-sum), [QM.3/bessel-j-bromwich-integral](#QM-3-bessel-j-bromwich-integral), [QM.2/modified-bessel-i-bromwich-integral](#QM-2-modified-bessel-i-bromwich-integral), [QM.2/bessel-function-j](#QM-2-bessel-function-j), [QM.2/modified-bessel-function-i](#QM-2-modified-bessel-function-i), `mathlib:hasSum_fourier_series_of_summable`, `mathlib:MeasureTheory.integral_prod`.

Acceptance checks:

- For N = 1, k = 12, m = 1: P(1, 12, 1) is a non-zero multiple of Δ, so a(1, 12, 1; n)/(1 + a(1, 12, 1; 1)) = τ(n) (checked numerically: truncating the c-sum at c < 4000 gives a(1, 12, 1; 1) ≈ 1.84029, a(2)/(1 + a(1)) = −24.000, a(3)/(1 + a(1)) = 252.000).
- m = 0 is excluded: then P(0, k, N) is the Eisenstein series at ∞, whose coefficients are divisor sums, not Bessel sums.

<a id="QM-3-maass-poincare-series-fourier-expansion"></a>

### Fourier expansion of Maass–Poincaré series

**Theorem** (`QM.3/maass-poincare-series-fourier-expansion`). For even k ≥ 4 and m, N ≥ 1: Q(−m, k, N) = Q⁺ + Q⁻ with Q⁻ = −Γ(k−1, 4πmv)q^{−m}/(k−2)! + Σ_{n<0} b(n)Γ(k−1, 4π|n|v)q^n and Q⁺ = q^{−m} + Σ_{n≥0} b(n)q^n, where for n < 0: b(n) = −2π(−1)^{k/2}/(k−2)!·|m/n|^{(k−1)/2}Σ_{c>0, N|c} K(−m, n, c)/c·J_{k−1}(4π√|mn|/c); b(0) = −(2π)^k(−1)^{k/2}m^{k−1}/(k−1)!·Σ_{c>0, N|c} K(−m, 0, c)/c^k; for n > 0: b(n) = −2π(−1)^{k/2}(m/n)^{(k−1)/2}Σ_{c>0, N|c} K(−m, n, c)/c·I_{k−1}(4π√(mn)/c) (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Prop. 6.2).

Ambient hypotheses: As in QM.3/maass-poincare-series. Here b(n) denotes the Bessel-sum correction after the seed is written separately: the total non-holomorphic coefficient at n<0 is −δ_{n,−m}/(k−2)! + b(n). The holomorphic q^{−m} seed is also separate..

Sources: [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), Prop. 6.2, p. 16; [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), Prop. 6.2, p. 16.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/maass-poincare-series](#QM-3-maass-poincare-series), [QM.3/maass-poincare-series-harmonic](#QM-3-maass-poincare-series-harmonic), [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion), [QM.3/xi-maass-poincare-series](#QM-3-xi-maass-poincare-series), [QM.3/xi-fourier-expansion](#QM-3-xi-fourier-expansion), [QM.3/bol-image-of-maass-poincare-series](#QM-3-bol-image-of-maass-poincare-series), [QM.3/flipping-derivative-theorem](#QM-3-flipping-derivative-theorem), [QM.3/holomorphic-poincare-series-fourier-expansion](#QM-3-holomorphic-poincare-series-fourier-expansion), [QM.3/classical-kloosterman-sum](#QM-3-classical-kloosterman-sum), `mathlib:MeasureTheory.integral_prod`.

Acceptance checks:

- N = 1, m = 1, k = 12: b(0) = −(2π)^{12}/(11!·ζ(12)) = −65520/691 (since K(−1, 0, c) = μ(c) and Σ_c μ(c)c^{−12} = 1/ζ(12)), b(1) ≈ −1842.89472, b(2) ≈ −23274.07545, b(3) ≈ −225028.75877 (numerically checked; these agree with BOR's list except its constant term, E405).
- Consistency with QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing-formula at level one: {E_k, Q(−m, k, 1)} = 0 gives b⁺(0) = (2k/B_k)σ_{k−1}(m), which equals the Kloosterman-sum formula because Σ_c K(−m, 0, c)c^{−k} = σ_{1−k}(m)/ζ(k) (Ramanujan sums).

<a id="QM-3-level-one-plus-space-spanned-by-poincare-series"></a>

### H_{2−k}^+(SL₂(ℤ)) is spanned by Maass–Poincaré series

**Theorem** (`QM.3/level-one-plus-space-spanned-by-poincare-series`). For even k ≥ 4: every f ∈ H_{2−k}^+(SL₂(ℤ)) is a finite linear combination Σ_{m=1}^{M} a⁺(−m)·Q(−m, k, 1) of Maass–Poincaré series (a⁺ its holomorphic coefficients). In particular f is determined by its principal part without constant term, and M^!_{2−k}(SL₂(ℤ)) ⊆ span{Q(−m, k, 1)} (Bruinier–Funke Remark 3.10, scalar level one).

Ambient hypotheses: Level one; weight 2 − k ≤ −2..

Sources: [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Remark 3.10, p. 15; [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), p. 16.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/maass-poincare-series-harmonic](#QM-3-maass-poincare-series-harmonic), [QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing-formula](#QM-3-bruinier-funke-pairing-formula), [QM.3/bruinier-funke-duality](#QM-3-bruinier-funke-duality), [QM.3/xi-kernel-weakly-holomorphic](#QM-3-xi-kernel-weakly-holomorphic), `mathlib:ModularFormClass.levelOne_neg_weight_eq_zero`.

Acceptance checks:

- dim(H_{−10}^+/M^!_{−10}) = 1 and Q(−1, 12, 1) spans it modulo M^!_{−10}.

<a id="QM-3-level-one-cusp-forms-spanned-by-poincare-series"></a>

### S_k(SL₂(ℤ)) is spanned by holomorphic Poincaré series

**Theorem** (`QM.3/level-one-cusp-forms-spanned-by-poincare-series`). For even k ≥ 4, S_k(SL₂(ℤ)) is spanned by {P(m, k, 1) : m ≥ 1}.

Ambient hypotheses: Level one, k even ≥ 4..

Sources: [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Remark 3.10, p. 15; [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), §6.2, p. 17.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/bruinier-funke-exact-sequences](#QM-3-bruinier-funke-exact-sequences), [QM.3/level-one-plus-space-spanned-by-poincare-series](#QM-3-level-one-plus-space-spanned-by-poincare-series), [QM.3/xi-maass-poincare-series](#QM-3-xi-maass-poincare-series), [QM.3/holomorphic-poincare-series](#QM-3-holomorphic-poincare-series).

Acceptance checks:

- k = 12: P(1, 12, 1) spans S_12 = ℂΔ.

<a id="QM-3-flipping-derivative-theorem"></a>

### D^{k−1} maps H_{2−k}^+ to weakly holomorphic forms (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Theorem 1.1)

**Theorem** (`QM.3/flipping-derivative-theorem`). Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ≥ 2 an integer and f ∈ H_{2−k}^+(Γ). Then D^{k−1}f ∈ M^!_k(Γ) (D = (2πi)^{−1}∂_τ), and at ∞ (width h) D^{k−1}f = D^{k−1}f⁺ = Σ_{n≫−∞} a⁺(n)(n/h)^{k−1}e(nτ/h); for h = 1 this is Σ a⁺(n)n^{k−1}q^n.

Ambient hypotheses: k ≥ 2; BOR state it for Γ₀(N) with character; the proof is the same for finite-index Γ..

Sources: [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), Theorem 1.1, p. 2; [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), proof of Thm 1.1, p. 8.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/bol-identity](#QM-3-bol-identity), [QM.3/iterated-raising-operator](#QM-3-iterated-raising-operator), [QM.3/raising-lowering-eigenvalue-shift](#QM-3-raising-lowering-eigenvalue-shift), [QM.3/laplacian-raising-lowering-factorisation](#QM-3-laplacian-raising-lowering-factorisation), [QM.3/maass-lowering-operator](#QM-3-maass-lowering-operator), [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion), [QM.3/holomorphic-part](#QM-3-holomorphic-part), [QM.3/weakly-holomorphic-modular-form](#QM-3-weakly-holomorphic-modular-form).

Acceptance checks:

- For f = Q(−m, k, N): D^{k−1}Q = −m^{k−1}P(−m, k, N) (QM.3/bol-image-of-maass-poincare-series).
- For f ∈ M^!_{2−k}: the classical fact that D^{k−1} maps M^!_{2−k} to M^!_k.

Proof or comparison obligations: Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades and Lewis–Zagier operator comparisons.

<a id="QM-3-bol-image-of-maass-poincare-series"></a>

### D^{k−1}Q(−m, k, N) = −m^{k−1}P(−m, k, N)

**Theorem** (`QM.3/bol-image-of-maass-poincare-series`). For even k ≥ 4 and m, N ≥ 1: D^{k−1}Q(−m, k, N) = −m^{k−1}·P(−m, k, N) (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades (6.8)).

Ambient hypotheses: As in QM.3/maass-poincare-series..

Sources: [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), (6.8), p. 16.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/flipping-derivative-theorem](#QM-3-flipping-derivative-theorem), [QM.3/bol-identity](#QM-3-bol-identity), [QM.3/maass-poincare-series](#QM-3-maass-poincare-series), [QM.3/holomorphic-poincare-series](#QM-3-holomorphic-poincare-series).

Acceptance checks:

- Coefficientwise: a⁺(n)n^{k−1} = −m^{k−1}a(−m, k, N; n), consistent with BOR Props. 6.1(2), 6.2.

<a id="QM-3-regularized-petersson-product"></a>

### The truncated (regularized) Petersson product

**Definition** (`QM.3/regularized-petersson-product`). Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index and k ∈ ℤ. For g ∈ M_k(Γ) and h ∈ M^!_k(Γ) with vanishing constant term at every cusp: (g, h)^{reg} := [SL₂(ℤ) : Γ]^{−1}·lim_{T→∞} ∫_{F_T(Γ)} g(τ)\overline{h(τ)}v^k dμ, where F_T(Γ) = ⋃_{γ ∈ Γ\SL₂(ℤ)} γF_T and F_T is the truncated standard fundamental domain. This is Borcherds' regularization (constant term at s = 0 of the continuation in s) in the case where no continuation is needed (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades §4, Remark 8); it reduces to the normalised Petersson product for cusp forms.

Ambient hypotheses: h has vanishing constant term at every cusp (otherwise the limit need not exist and Borcherds' meromorphic continuation in s is required; that general regularization is not planned here).; Normalisation: divided by the index [SL₂(ℤ) : Γ] (BOR), unlike QM.3/bruinier-funke-pairing..

Sources: [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), §4, p. 9; [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), Remark 8, p. 9.

Direct prerequisites: `mathlib:ModularForm`, `mathlib:ModularGroup.fd`, `tauceti:UpperHalfPlane.peterssonInner`, [QM.3/weakly-holomorphic-laurent-expansion](#QM-3-weakly-holomorphic-laurent-expansion).

Named declarations and API:

- `regularizedPetersson` (data): (g, h)^{reg} = [SL₂(ℤ):Γ]^{−1} lim_T ∫_{F_T(Γ)} g\overline{h}v^k dμ.
- `regularizedPetersson_tendsto` (other): The truncated integrals converge when h has zero constant terms at all cusps.
- `regularizedPetersson_eq_of_isCuspForm` (compatibility): For h a cusp form it is the index-normalised Petersson product.

Unit tests:

- `regularizedPetersson_cuspForm_test` (compatibility): For g, h ∈ S_k(Γ) the regularized product equals the (index-normalised) Petersson product.
- `regularizedPetersson_zero_test` (degenerate): (g, 0)^{reg} = 0.
- `regularizedPetersson_bol_test` (computation): Level one, k = 12: (Δ, D^{11}Q(−1, 12, 1))^{reg} = 0 (QM.3/regularized-pairing-with-bol-image with vanishing cusp-form constant term).
- `regularizedPetersson_ne_test` (non-example): For g = h = E₁₂ (constant term 1) the truncated integrals ∫_{F_T}|E₁₂|²v^{12}dμ grow like T^{11}/11: the hypothesis on constant terms cannot be dropped.

Acceptance checks:

- For g, h ∈ S_k(Γ): (g, h)^{reg} = [SL₂(ℤ) : Γ]^{−1}·Tau Ceti's CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets h g (the same integral; Tau Ceti is conjugate-linear in h and linear in g).

<a id="QM-3-regularized-pairing-with-bol-image"></a>

### (g, R^{k−1}_{2−k}f)^{reg} via constant terms (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Theorem 4.1, corrected)

**Theorem** (`QM.3/regularized-pairing-with-bol-image`). Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, k ≥ 2, g ∈ M_k(Γ), f ∈ H_{2−k}^+(Γ). Then (g, R^{k−1}_{2−k}f)^{reg} = ((−1)^k(k−2)!/[SL₂(ℤ) : Γ])·Σ_{κ ∈ Γ\ℙ¹(ℚ)} w_κ·c_g(0, κ)·\overline{c⁺_f(0, κ)}, where c_g(0, κ), c⁺_f(0, κ) are the constant terms at the cusp κ and w_κ its width. BOR print the formula without the factor (k−2)! (sourceIssue E408). In particular (g, D^{k−1}f)^{reg} = 0 for cusp forms g (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Cor. 4.2).

Ambient hypotheses: k ≥ 2; h := R^{k−1}_{2−k}f = (−4π)^{k−1}D^{k−1}f ∈ M^!_k has vanishing constant terms (coefficients a⁺(n)(−4πn)^{k−1}), so the truncated product is defined..

Sources: [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), Theorem 4.1, p. 9; [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), proof of Thm 4.1, p. 10.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/regularized-petersson-product](#QM-3-regularized-petersson-product), [QM.3/flipping-derivative-theorem](#QM-3-flipping-derivative-theorem), [QM.3/iterated-raising-operator](#QM-3-iterated-raising-operator), [QM.3/truncated-fundamental-domain-stokes](#QM-3-truncated-fundamental-domain-stokes), [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-fourier-expansion), [QM.3/xi-xi-eq-neg-laplacian](#QM-3-xi-xi-eq-neg-laplacian).

Acceptance checks:

- For g ∈ S_k(Γ): (g, D^{k−1}f)^{reg} = 0 (BOR Cor. 4.2).
- For k = 2 the factor (k−2)! = 1 and BOR's formula is correct as printed.

<a id="QM-3-image-of-bol-operator"></a>

### The image of D^{k−1} on H_{2−k}^+ (Bruinier–Ono–Rhoades Theorem 1.2 / Corollary 4.3)

**Theorem** (`QM.3/image-of-bol-operator`). Let Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) have finite index and k ≥ 2. The image of D^{k−1} : H_{2−k}^+(Γ) → M^!_k(Γ) consists exactly of those h ∈ M^!_k(Γ) with vanishing constant term at every cusp and (g, h)^{reg} = 0 for all g ∈ S_k(Γ).

Ambient hypotheses: k ≥ 2; Γ of finite index..

Sources: [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), Cor. 4.3, p. 10; [bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008](#reference-bruinier-ono-rhoades-2008), Theorem 1.2, p. 2.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/regularized-pairing-with-bol-image](#QM-3-regularized-pairing-with-bol-image), [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-prescribed-principal-parts](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-prescribed-principal-parts), [QM.3/flipping-derivative-theorem](#QM-3-flipping-derivative-theorem), [QM.3/regularized-petersson-product](#QM-3-regularized-petersson-product).

Acceptance checks:

- BOR §7: m(z) = (η(z)³/η(9z)³ + 3)²η(3z)⁸ ∈ M^!_4(Γ₀(9)) equals −D³Q(−1, 4, 9) (= P(−1, 4, 9)).

<a id="QM-3-nonholomorphic-eisenstein-series-e2-star"></a>

### The non-holomorphic Eisenstein series E₂*

**Construction** (`QM.3/nonholomorphic-eisenstein-series-e2-star`). E₂*(τ) := E₂(τ) − 3/(πv), with Mathlib's E₂ = EisensteinSeries.E2 (= 1 − 24Σσ₁(n)q^n). It is SL₂(ℤ)-invariant of weight 2, harmonic (Δ_2(v^{−1}) = 0), of moderate growth, hence E₂* ∈ H_2(SL₂(ℤ)), and ξ_2E₂* = 3/π. Since 3/π is not a cusp form, E₂* ∉ H_2^+(SL₂(ℤ)).

Ambient hypotheses: Level one, weight 2 (the case k ≥ 2 of the first exact sequence, where ξ_2 maps onto M^!_0)..

Sources: [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), §3, p. 9; [bruinier-funke-2004](#reference-bruinier-funke-2004), Cor. 3.8, p. 15.

Direct prerequisites: `mathlib:EisensteinSeries.E2`, `mathlib:EisensteinSeries.E2_slash_action`, `mathlib:EisensteinSeries.D2`, `mathlib:E2_mdifferentiable`, `mathlib:EisensteinSeries.E2_eq_tsum_cexp`, [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form), [QM.3/xi-map](#QM-3-xi-map), [QM.3/weight-k-hyperbolic-laplacian](#QM-3-weight-k-hyperbolic-laplacian), [QM.3/harmonic-maass-form-plus-space](#QM-3-harmonic-maass-form-plus-space).

Named declarations and API:

- `e2Star` (data): E₂*(τ) = E₂(τ) − 3/(π Im τ).
- `e2Star_slash` (characterisation): E₂*|_2γ = E₂* for γ ∈ SL₂(ℤ).
- `e2StarHarmonic` (constructor): E₂* as an element of H_2(SL₂(ℤ)).
- `xiOperator_e2Star` (simp): ξ_2E₂* = 3/π.
- `e2Star_not_mem_plusSpace` (other): E₂* ∉ H_2^+(SL₂(ℤ)).

Unit tests:

- `e2Star_slash_test` (characterisation): E₂*|_2γ = E₂* for every γ ∈ SL₂(ℤ).
- `e2Star_i_test` (computation): E₂*(i) = 0, i.e. E₂(i) = 3/π.
- `e2Star_ne_E2_test` (non-example): E₂* ≠ E₂ and E₂ itself is not SL₂(ℤ)-invariant of weight 2.
- `xi_e2Star_const_test` (compatibility): ξ_2(E₂*) = 3/π, the ξ-image of −(3/π)v^{−1}.

Acceptance checks:

- E₂*(i) = E₂(i) − 3/π = 0 (from the S-invariance of E₂* at the fixed point i: E₂*(i) = i^{−2}E₂*(i)).


## QM.4 Mock modular completions

The error-function correction to Appell–Lerch sums gives explicit elliptic and modular laws. Indefinite theta functions separate holomorphic sign terms from nonholomorphic beta terms, with convergence on their admissible domains. Seventh- and fifth-order vectors apply this machinery with exact characteristics and roots of unity. Eulerian identifications and growth-free torsion comparisons carry their stated proof gaps.

**Coverage: planned.**

The open targets and comparisons for this layer are:

- The selected seventh-order completion nodes use indefinite double sums; the recorded Hickerson gap is still required to identify them with Ramanujan’s Eulerian series. Do not infer that identity from the bounded coefficient check.
- The recorded torsion-specialization gap still requires Jacobi transformation laws without a growth condition, on the precise finite-index subgroup. Resolve the canonical Jacobi supplier/import comparison before closing residue-function-modularity; the local QM.1 interface is not newly verified in this pass.
- Fifth-order: prove the Andrews Eulerian/double-sum identifications with convergence, denominator nonvanishing and interchange. The coordinates of H₁,G₁,H₂,G₂,F₂ and the S/T matrices are now specified in the existing nodes and native signatures. No congruence kernel or classical Eulerian identity follows merely from those signatures. QM.4 is planned with the stated proof gaps, not closed.
- Complete the theorem/section/page and supplier comparisons in: Finite Weil, Kohnen and multivariate Poisson supplier comparisons. Each gap gives the affected node ids and their exact source/supplier worklist.

<a id="QM-4-zwegers-error-function"></a>

### Zwegers' error function E(x)

**Definition** (`QM.4/zwegers-error-function`). For x ∈ ℝ, E(x) := 2∫_0^x e^{−πu²}du = erf(√π·x), where erf = TauCeti.Real.erf. E is odd, increasing, E(x) → ±1 as x → ±∞, E′(x) = 2e^{−πx²}, and E(x) = Σ_{n≥0}(−π)^n x^{2n+1}/(n!(n + 1/2)) (Zwegers Def. 1.6). Zwegers defines E as an entire function of z ∈ ℂ, but every use in the thesis (R, R_{m,l}, ρ^c) evaluates it at real arguments, so the real function is the object built here.

Ambient hypotheses: Real variable only; the entire extension is not needed by any node..

Sources: [zwegers-thesis](#reference-zwegers-thesis), Def. 1.6, p. 11.

Direct prerequisites: `tauceti:TauCeti.Real.erf`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Real.erf_neg`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Real.hasDerivAt_erf`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Real.tendsto_erf_atTop`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Real.tendsto_erf_atBot`.

Named declarations and API:

- `zwegersE` (data): E(x) = 2∫_0^x e^{−πu²}du.
- `zwegersE_eq_erf` (compatibility): E(x) = TauCeti.Real.erf(√π x).
- `zwegersE_neg` (simp): E(−x) = −E(x).
- `hasDerivAt_zwegersE` (other): E′(x) = 2e^{−πx²}.
- `abs_zwegersE_lt_one` (other): |E(x)| < 1.
- `tendsto_zwegersE_atTop` (other): E(x) → 1 as x → ∞ (and → −1 as x → −∞).

Unit tests:

- `zwegersE_zero_test` (degenerate): E(0) = 0.
- `zwegersE_eq_erf_test` (compatibility): E(x) = TauCeti.Real.erf(√π·x) for all real x.
- `zwegersE_deriv_test` (computation): E′(0) = 2 (a definition with erf(x) instead of erf(√π x) would give 2/√π).
- `zwegersE_tendsto_test` (characterisation): E(x) → 1 as x → +∞ and E(x) → −1 as x → −∞.

Acceptance checks:

- E(0) = 0, E′(0) = 2, E(x) → 1 as x → ∞.
- |E(x)| < 1 for all real x.

<a id="QM-4-zwegers-beta-function"></a>

### Zwegers' function β(x)

**Definition** (`QM.4/zwegers-beta-function`). For x ≥ 0, β(x) := ∫_x^∞ u^{−1/2}e^{−πu}du = erfc(√(πx)); for x>0 also β(x)=π^{−1/2}Γ(1/2, πx) (Zwegers Lemma 1.7), with Γ(s, x) the upper incomplete gamma function (QM.3/upper-incomplete-gamma). It satisfies β(0) = 1, 0 ≤ β(x) ≤ e^{−πx}, β decreasing, β′(x) = −x^{−1/2}e^{−πx} for x > 0.

Ambient hypotheses: x ≥ 0 (β(0) = 1 via Γ(1/2) = √π); totalised by β(x) := 1 for x < 0 is not used.; QM.3 totalizes upperIncompleteGamma(s,0) to 0. Thus the identity with upperIncompleteGamma is restricted to x>0; β(0)=1 uses the complete Gamma value or erfc(0), not that totalized value..

Sources: [zwegers-thesis](#reference-zwegers-thesis), Lemma 1.7, p. 11; [zwegers-thesis](#reference-zwegers-thesis), proof of Lemma 1.8, p. 12.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.3/upper-incomplete-gamma](#QM-3-upper-incomplete-gamma), `tauceti:TauCeti.Real.erfc`, `mathlib:Real.Gamma_one_half_eq`.

Named declarations and API:

- `zwegersBeta` (data): β(x) = ∫_{(x,∞)} u^{−1/2}e^{−πu}du.
- `zwegersBeta_eq_upperIncompleteGamma` (compatibility): β(x) = π^{−1/2}Γ(1/2, πx) for x > 0.
- `zwegersBeta_eq_erfc` (compatibility): β(x) = erfc(√(πx)) for x ≥ 0.
- `zwegersBeta_le_exp` (other): 0 ≤ β(x) ≤ e^{−πx}.
- `tendsto_zwegersBeta_atTop` (other): β(x) → 0 as x → ∞.

Unit tests:

- `zwegersBeta_zero_test` (degenerate): β(0) = 1.
- `zwegersBeta_eq_erfc_test` (compatibility): β(x) = TauCeti.Real.erfc(√(πx)) for x ≥ 0.
- `zwegersBeta_le_exp_test` (characterisation): 0 ≤ β(x) ≤ e^{−πx} for x ≥ 0.
- `zwegersBeta_ne_upper_gamma_test` (non-example): β(1) = π^{−1/2}Γ(1/2, π) ≠ Γ(1/2, 1): the argument is scaled by π.

Acceptance checks:

- β(0) = 1 and β(x) ≤ e^{−πx}, the two facts used in every convergence proof of Zwegers Ch. 1–4.

<a id="QM-4-error-function-sign-beta"></a>

### E(x) = sgn(x)(1 − β(x²)) (Zwegers Lemma 1.7)

**Lemma** (`QM.4/error-function-sign-beta`). For every real x: E(x) = sgn(x)·(1 − β(x²)).

Ambient hypotheses: sgn(0) = 0, consistent with E(0) = 0..

Sources: [zwegers-thesis](#reference-zwegers-thesis), Lemma 1.7, p. 11.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.4/zwegers-error-function](#QM-4-zwegers-error-function), [QM.4/zwegers-beta-function](#QM-4-zwegers-beta-function).

Acceptance checks:

- At x = 0 both sides vanish; for x → ∞, β(x²) → 0.

<a id="QM-4-mordell-integral"></a>

### The Mordell integral h(z; τ)

**Definition** (`QM.4/mordell-integral`). For z ∈ ℂ and τ ∈ ℍ, h(z; τ) := ∫_ℝ e^{πiτx² − 2πzx}/cosh(πx) dx (Zwegers Def. 1.1). The integral converges absolutely (|e^{πiτx²}| = e^{−πyx²}) and h is entire in z and holomorphic in τ.

Ambient hypotheses: τ ∈ ℍ; z ∈ ℂ arbitrary..

Sources: [zwegers-thesis](#reference-zwegers-thesis), Def. 1.1, p. 6.

Direct prerequisites: `mathlib:Real.cosh`, `mathlib:Complex.cosh`, `mathlib:hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le`.

Named declarations and API:

- `mordellIntegral` (data): h(z; τ) = ∫_ℝ e^{πiτx² − 2πzx}/cosh(πx)dx.
- `mordellIntegral_neg` (simp): h(−z; τ) = h(z; τ) (Zwegers Prop. 1.2(4)).
- `differentiable_mordellIntegral` (other): z ↦ h(z; τ) is entire.
- `mordellIntegral_integrable` (other): The integrand is integrable for τ ∈ ℍ.

Unit tests:

- `mordellIntegral_neg_test` (characterisation): h(−z; τ) = h(z; τ).
- `mordellIntegral_shift_test` (computation): h(z; τ) + h(z + 1; τ) = (−iτ)^{−1/2}·2e^{πi(z+1/2)²/τ} (principal branch).
- `mordellIntegral_zero_i_pos_test` (degenerate): h(0; i) is real and positive.
- `mordellIntegral_not_periodic_test` (non-example): h is not 1-periodic in z: h(0; i) + h(1; i) = 2e^{π/4} while 0 < h(0; i) ≤ ∫e^{−πx²}dx = 1 < e^{π/4}, so h(1; i) ≠ h(0; i).

Acceptance checks:

- h(0; i) = ∫e^{−πx²}/cosh(πx)dx > 0 and h is even in z.

<a id="QM-4-mordell-integral-translation-one"></a>

### h(z) + h(z + 1) = 2(−iτ)^{−1/2}e^{πi(z+1/2)²/τ} (Zwegers Prop. 1.2(1))

**Lemma** (`QM.4/mordell-integral-translation-one`). For τ ∈ ℍ, z ∈ ℂ: h(z; τ) + h(z + 1; τ) = (2/√(−iτ))·e^{πi(z + 1/2)²/τ}, with the principal branch of the square root (Re √(−iτ) > 0).

Ambient hypotheses: √(−iτ) principal (−iτ has positive real part)..

Sources: [zwegers-thesis](#reference-zwegers-thesis), Prop. 1.2(1), p. 6.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.4/mordell-integral](#QM-4-mordell-integral), `mathlib:integral_cexp_quadratic`.

Acceptance checks:

- With z = −1/2 and h even: h(1/2; τ) = (−iτ)^{−1/2}.

<a id="QM-4-mordell-integral-translation-tau"></a>

### h(z) + e^{−2πiz−πiτ}h(z + τ) = 2e^{−πiz−πiτ/4} (Zwegers Prop. 1.2(2))

**Lemma** (`QM.4/mordell-integral-translation-tau`). For τ ∈ ℍ, z ∈ ℂ: h(z) + e^{−2πiz − πiτ}h(z + τ) = 2e^{−πiz − πiτ/4}.

Ambient hypotheses: τ ∈ ℍ..

Sources: [zwegers-thesis](#reference-zwegers-thesis), Prop. 1.2(2), p. 6.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.4/mordell-integral](#QM-4-mordell-integral).

Acceptance checks:

- Together with Prop. 1.2(1) this determines h (Prop. 1.2(3)).

<a id="QM-4-mordell-integral-uniqueness"></a>

### Uniqueness of solutions of the two functional equations (Zwegers Prop. 1.2(3))

**Lemma** (`QM.4/mordell-integral-uniqueness`). For fixed τ ∈ ℍ, z ↦ h(z; τ) is the unique holomorphic function f on ℂ with f(z) + f(z + 1) = 2(−iτ)^{−1/2}e^{πi(z+1/2)²/τ} and f(z) + e^{−2πiz−πiτ}f(z + τ) = 2e^{−πiz−πiτ/4} for all z.

Ambient hypotheses: τ ∈ ℍ fixed..

Sources: [zwegers-thesis](#reference-zwegers-thesis), Prop. 1.2(3), p. 6.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.4/mordell-integral](#QM-4-mordell-integral), [QM.4/mordell-integral-translation-one](#QM-4-mordell-integral-translation-one), [QM.4/mordell-integral-translation-tau](#QM-4-mordell-integral-translation-tau), `mathlib:Differentiable.apply_eq_apply_of_bounded`.

Acceptance checks:

- Used for Prop. 1.2(5), (6), Prop. 1.5(2) and Prop. 1.10(2).

### h(z/τ; −1/τ) = √(−iτ)e^{−πiz²/τ}h(z; τ) (Zwegers Prop. 1.2(5))

**Theorem** (`QM.4/mordell-integral-s-transformation`). For τ ∈ ℍ, z ∈ ℂ: h(z/τ; −1/τ) = √(−iτ)·e^{−πiz²/τ}·h(z; τ).

Ambient hypotheses: Principal square root..

Sources: [zwegers-thesis](#reference-zwegers-thesis), Prop. 1.2(5), p. 6.

<a id="QM-4-mordell-integral-t-transformation"></a>

### The τ ↦ τ + 1 relation for h (Zwegers Prop. 1.2(6))

**Lemma** (`QM.4/mordell-integral-t-transformation`). For τ ∈ ℍ, z ∈ ℂ: h(z; τ) = e^{πi/4}h(z; τ + 1) + (e^{−πi/4}/√(τ + 1))·e^{πiz²/(τ+1)}·h(z/(τ + 1); τ/(τ + 1)).

<a id="QM-4-appell-lerch-sum"></a>

### The Appell–Lerch sum μ(u, v; τ)

**Definition** (`QM.4/appell-lerch-sum`). For τ ∈ ℍ and u, v ∈ ℂ \ (ℤτ + ℤ): μ(u, v; τ) := (e^{πiu}/ϑ(v; τ))·Σ_{n∈ℤ} (−1)^n e^{πi(n²+n)τ + 2πinv}/(1 − e^{2πinτ + 2πiu}) (Zwegers Prop. 1.4, the normalised Lerch sum). The series converges absolutely and locally uniformly on u ∉ ℤτ + ℤ (the numerator decays like e^{−πn²y}); as a function of u it is meromorphic with simple poles at ℤτ + ℤ.

Ambient hypotheses: u, v ∉ ℤτ + ℤ (ϑ(v) ≠ 0 by QM.1/jacobi-theta-zeros); junk value 0 elsewhere in the Lean definition..

Sources: [zwegers-thesis](#reference-zwegers-thesis), Prop. 1.4, p. 8; [zwegers-thesis](#reference-zwegers-thesis), Introduction, p. 3.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.1/jacobi-theta-function](#QM-1-jacobi-theta-function), [QM.1/jacobi-theta-zeros](#QM-1-jacobi-theta-zeros).

Named declarations and API:

- `appellLerch` (data): μ(u, v; τ) = e^{πiu}ϑ(v; τ)^{−1}Σ_n (−1)^n e^{πi(n²+n)τ+2πinv}/(1 − e^{2πinτ+2πiu}).
- `appellLerch_summable` (other): The defining series converges absolutely, locally uniformly for u ∉ ℤτ + ℤ.
- `oddJacobiTheta_mul_appellLerch` (characterisation): ϑ(v; τ)·μ(u, v; τ) = e^{πiu}Σ_n (−1)^n e^{πi(n²+n)τ+2πinv}/(1 − e^{2πinτ+2πiu}) (Lerch's sum).
- `meromorphic_appellLerch` (other): u ↦ μ(u, v; τ) is meromorphic on ℂ with poles in ℤτ + ℤ.

Unit tests:

- `appellLerch_symm_test` (characterisation): μ(u, v; τ) = μ(v, u; τ) for u, v ∉ ℤτ + ℤ.
- `appellLerch_residue_test` (computation): lim_{u→0} u·μ(u, v; τ) = −1/(2πi ϑ(v; τ)).
- `appellLerch_neg_test` (characterisation): μ(−u, −v) = μ(u, v).
- `appellLerch_not_elliptic_test` (non-example): μ(u + τ, v) ≠ −e^{2πi(u−v)+πiτ}μ(u, v) in general: by Prop. 1.4(3) the defect is −ie^{−πi(u−v)−πiτ/4}·e^{2πi(u−v)+πiτ} ≠ 0; only μ̃ is elliptic.

Acceptance checks:

- μ(u, v) = μ(v, u) (Prop. 1.4(8)) although the definition is not visibly symmetric.
- Residue −1/(2πiϑ(v)) at u = 0.

Atlas planet: **Appell–Lerch sum μ(u, v; τ)**.

Ambient hypotheses: u, v ∉ ℤτ + ℤ..

Sources: [zwegers-thesis](#reference-zwegers-thesis), Prop. 1.4(1), p. 8.

<a id="QM-4-appell-lerch-translation-v-one"></a>

### μ(u, v + 1) = −μ(u, v) (Zwegers Prop. 1.4(2))

**Lemma** (`QM.4/appell-lerch-translation-v-one`). μ(u, v + 1; τ) = −μ(u, v; τ).

Ambient hypotheses: u, v ∉ ℤτ + ℤ..

Sources: [zwegers-thesis](#reference-zwegers-thesis), Prop. 1.4(2), p. 9.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.4/appell-lerch-sum](#QM-4-appell-lerch-sum), [QM.1/jacobi-theta-elliptic](#QM-1-jacobi-theta-elliptic).

Acceptance checks:

- —

<a id="QM-4-appell-lerch-translation-tau"></a>

### μ(u, v) + e^{−2πi(u−v)−πiτ}μ(u + τ, v) = −ie^{−πi(u−v)−πiτ/4} (Zwegers Prop. 1.4(3))

**Lemma** (`QM.4/appell-lerch-translation-tau`). For u, v, u + τ ∉ ℤτ + ℤ: μ(u, v) + e^{−2πi(u−v)−πiτ}μ(u + τ, v) = −i e^{−πi(u−v)−πiτ/4}.

Ambient hypotheses: u, v ∉ ℤτ + ℤ..

Sources: [zwegers-thesis](#reference-zwegers-thesis), Prop. 1.4(3), p. 9.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.4/appell-lerch-sum](#QM-4-appell-lerch-sum), [QM.1/jacobi-theta-function](#QM-1-jacobi-theta-function).

Acceptance checks:

- Combined with Prop. 1.9(2) it shows μ̃ is elliptic in u.

<a id="QM-4-appell-lerch-diagonal-translation"></a>

### μ(u + τ, v + τ) = μ(u, v) (Zwegers Prop. 1.4(4))

**Lemma** (`QM.4/appell-lerch-diagonal-translation`). μ(u + τ, v + τ) = μ(u, v).

Ambient hypotheses: u, v ∉ ℤτ + ℤ..

Sources: [zwegers-thesis](#reference-zwegers-thesis), Prop. 1.4(4), p. 9.

Direct prerequisites: [QM.4/appell-lerch-sum](#QM-4-appell-lerch-sum), [QM.1/jacobi-theta-elliptic](#QM-1-jacobi-theta-elliptic).
